ai_overview:
You can make a vibrant sourdough starter from scratch in 7 to 10 days using only unbleached flour, water, and daily feedings. What You Need Unbleached flour : Whole wheat or rye flour for Day 1, and unbleached all-purpose or bread flour for later feedings. Water : Filtered, bottled, or boiled and cooled water (around 75–80°F). Equipment : A clean glass jar, a kitchen scale, and a loose-fitting lid or cloth cover. Step-by-Step Schedule Day 1 (Initial Mix) :Place your jar on the scale and set it to zero.
Add 50g to 60g of whole wheat or rye flour and an equal weight (50g to 60g) of lukewarm water.
Stir until smooth like a thick pancake batter with no dry spots.
Cover loosely and let it sit at room temperature (70–80°F) for 24 hours. Place your jar on the scale and set it to zero. Add 50g to 60g of whole wheat or rye flour and an equal weight (50g to 60g) of lukewarm water. Stir until smooth like a thick pancake batter with no dry spots. Cover loosely and let it sit at room temperature (70–80°F) for 24 hours. Day 2 (First Feeding) :Discard about half of the mixture (down to roughly 50g).
Add 50g to 60g of all-purpose or bread flour and 50g to 60g of water.
Stir well, cover loosely, and rest for 24 hours. Discard about half of the mixture (down to roughly 50g). Add 50g to 60g of all-purpose or bread flour and 50g to 60g of water. Stir well, cover loosely, and rest for 24 hours. Days 3 through 7 (Daily Maintenance) :Repeat the exact same process once a day: discard half your starter, then feed with 60g fresh flour and 60g water.
Tip : Track the rise with a rubber band around the jar right after feeding. Repeat the exact same process once a day: discard half your starter, then feed with 60g fresh flour and 60g water. Day 7 and Onward (Readiness) :Your starter is ready when it predictably doubles or triples in size within 4 to 6 hours of a feeding, smells pleasantly yeasty/tangy, and looks bubbly and spongy.
